positions.name: BareErasureDirective
positions.frame: When a speaker commands that knowledge or a named decision be forgotten/removed outright, with no rationale offered and no alternative (revision, supersession) proposed, what does that imperative rest its authority on?
positions.why: Both expressions are bare imperatives ('Forget…', 'Remove all knowledge…') aimed at erasing rather than revising or superseding prior material — the relational and power reads both flag the same pattern (authority-ranking, legitimate/pressure, and a shared BareImperativeDirective/DirectiveKnowledgeErasure directional mint) across both segments, and the conviction read marks both as settled, non-argued instructions expecting compliance. The two-segment set coheres tightly enough to warrant a single frame: neither offers justification, consultation, or softened register — the directive form itself is the shared object of the read, independent of what each individually names (an unfound 'Quantum Widget Decision' vs. an unfound migration topic, per the settled bindings marking both 'new'/absent from the graph).
